title: Chapter 1.  Geography — Location, Extent & Physiographic Divisions

blocks.content: Jammu and Kashmir's geography is exceptionally rich in exam content because very few Indian territories combine such extreme relief (from sub-tropical Jammu plains to the cold desert of the Karakoram) within one administrative unit. This chapter lays out the overall physiographic framework before the following three chapters go deep on mountain ranges, valleys/glaciers, and rivers/climate respectively.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: India lies completely in the Northern and Eastern Hemispheres, ranking as the 7th largest country by land area worldwide.
The Tropic of Cancer (23°30'N) divides the nation into roughly equal tropical and sub-tropical zones.
The country consists of six distinct physiographic divisions: Himalayan Mountains, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Indian Desert, Coastal Plains, and Islands.
India's Standard Meridian (82°30'E) determines Indian Standard Time (IST), operating 5 hours and 30 minutes ahead of GMT.
The Peninsular Plateau represents the oldest and most stable geological block of India, derived from ancient Gondwanaland.

blocks.content: The Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir lies in the north-westernmost part of India, in the outer and middle ranges of the Himalayas, bordered by Pakistan-administered territory to the west and north-west, the Union Territory of Ladakh to the east and north-east, Himachal Pradesh to the south-east, and Punjab to the south.

J&K's location gives it an intensely strategic character: it lies at the meeting point of the Indian subcontinent, Central Asia, and the Tibetan plateau, historically making it a corridor for trade, migration and military movement, and in the present day, a zone of persistent geopolitical sensitivity due to its proximity to the Line of Control (LoC) with Pakistan.
Chapter 1. Geography — Location, Extent & Physiographic Divisions

The Line of Control (LoC) is the de facto military boundary separating Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir from Pakistan-administered territory, established after the 1948 and 1971 conflicts and formalised in its present alignment by the Simla Agreement of 1972. India's official position is that the entire former princely state, including Pakistan-administered areas, is an integral part of India; Pakistan disputes this and administers its portion separately. This remains a live, internationally watched territorial dispute, and candidates should present it as an unresolved bilateral issue rather than a settled matter.

cells: approx 42,241 sq km (Jammu division approx 26,293 sq km; Kashmir division approx 15,948 sq km) - Indian-administered territory only, excluding Pakistan-administered areas and the separate UT of Ladakh
The historic biannual shifting of the seat of government between Srinagar (summer) and Jammu (winter), dating to Dogra rule and continued in the present UT
20 (10 in Jammu division, 10 in Kashmir division)

rows: High elevation peaks, deep V-shaped valleys
Relatively lower elevation, broad shallow valleys
Perennial, snow-fed rivers with high erosional activity
Peninsular seasonal rivers dependent mainly on rainfall

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: The 'Durbar Move' - the twice-yearly relocation of the secretariat between Jammu and Srinagar - is a distinctive administrative practice and a frequently tested one-liner; it has periodically been criticised for its cost, and reform proposals have surfaced repeatedly without full implementation.

J&K's terrain can be broadly divided into three major physiographic zones running roughly parallel in a north-west to south-east direction: the Outer Plains and Shivalik foothills of the Jammu region in the south; the Pir Panjal mountain zone and the intervening Kashmir Valley in the centre; and the high Himalayan zone bordering Ladakh in the north and east.

This layered rise in elevation - from sub-tropical plains near the Punjab border (as low as 300 m) to permanently snow-bound peaks exceeding 7,000 m along the frontier - is one of the sharpest elevation gradients found within any single Indian state or UT, and underlies nearly all of the region's distinctive climate, vegetation and settlement patterns covered later in this chapter group.

items: Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.
The Standard Meridian (82°30'E) passes through 5 states: Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh.
Indira Point (6°45'N) in Great Nicobar is the southernmost point of the Indian Union, whereas Kanyakumari is the southernmost tip of the mainland.
The longitudinal difference between easternmost Arunachal Pradesh and westernmost Gujarat results in a 2-hour local time difference.

cells: Sub-tropical, agriculturally productive plains adjoining Punjab, drained by the Chenab, Tawi and other rivers
Low, geologically young foothills forming the outermost Himalayan range in the Jammu region
Includes the fertile, bowl-shaped Kashmir Valley (~1,600 m) ringed by the Pir Panjal and Great Himalayan/Zanskar ranges
Permanently snow-bound high peaks and passes along the frontier with Ladakh and LoC-adjacent areas

items: J&K (UT): approx 42,241 sq km; borders Pakistan (LoC) and the Indian territories Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and Punjab.
Srinagar = summer capital; Jammu = winter capital; the biannual shift is called the 'Durbar Move'.
20 districts total: 10 in Jammu division, 10 in Kashmir division.
Terrain rises in three broad zones: Outer Plains/Shivalik (south) -> Pir Panjal/Kashmir Valley (centre) -> High Himalayan zone (north/east).
The Line of Control (LoC) with Pakistan was formalised by the Simla Agreement, 1972; it remains a live, internationally watched territorial dispute.
